stops.note: probably from an Iranian source; the island of Rhodes was linked with the flower and put a rose on its coins
Romans scattered petals at banquets and honoured the dead at the spring Rosalia festival

borrowed into Old English and reinforced by Old French rose; the 'Wars of the Roses' (1455-87), after the Lancastrian red and Yorkist white roses, is a name popularised centuries later by Walter Scott

current_meaning: a prickly shrub with fragrant flowers; a pinkish colour
